title: 3D Analysis of Multi-cellular Responses to Chemoattractant Gradients
protocol: Design the mask of the mold for PDMS device using a 3D CAD software.
Print the mold using stereolithography equipment with a thermal resistant resin.
Mix thoroughly a PDMS monomer solution with the curing agent in a 10:1 ratio.
Degass the mixture by applying vacuum for 1 hour in a vacuum desiccator.
Dab the surface of the mold with an adhesive tape to remove dust.
Pour the degassed PDMS mixture into the mold.
If bubbles are present, repeat degassing in the vacuum desiccator.
Remove trapped bubbles between pillars using a sharp needle.
Cure the PDMS by heating at 80 °C for 2 hours.
Allow the cured PDMS to cool down at room temperature.
Cut the boundary between the mold and PDMS carefully with a blade.
Peel off the PDMS from the mold gently.
Trim the PDMS part to fit a 22 mm x 22 mm coverslip.
Punch a hole at the inlet of the trimmed PDMS part.
Clean the PDMS part and 22 mm x 22 mm coverslip by wiping the surfaces with low-lint tissues and 70% ethanol.
Remove large dust particles by dabbing with an adhesive tape.
Sterilize the PDMS part and coverslip by autoclaving (121 °C for 8 minutes wet, 15 minutes dry) or exposure to UV light for 1 hour.
Treat the bottom surface of the PDMS part and cover slip with corona discharge gun for 5 min in the tissue culture hood.
Bond the treated PDMS part and coverslip together.
Inject collagen into the device immediately after treatment within 5 minutes.
Mince the mammary gland tissue of mice with a scalpel until the tissue relaxes.

Shake minced tissue for 30 min at 37 °C in 50 mL of collagenase/trypsin solution (10 mL per mouse) in DEME/F12 supplemented with 0.1 g of trypsin, 0.1 g of collagenase, 5 mL of FBS, 250 μL of 1 μg/mL insulin, and 50 μL of 50 μg/mL gentamicin.
Centrifuge the collagenase/trypsin solution at 1,250 x g for 10 min.
Remove the supernatant by aspiration.
Disperse cells in 10 mL of DMEM/F12.
Centrifuge at 1,250 x g for 10 min.
Aspirate the DMEM/F12.
Re-suspend cells in 4 mL of DMEM/F12 supplemented with 40 μL of DNase (2 units/μL).
Shake the DNase solution by hand for 2-5 min.
Centrifuge at 1,250 x g for 10 min.
Separate organoids from single cells through four differential centrifugations.
Pulse to 1,250 x g and stop the centrifuge 3-4 s after it reaches speed.
Aspirate the supernatant between each pulse.
Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of DMEM/F12.
Re-suspend the final pellet in the desired amount of growth medium of DMEM/F12 with 1% penicillin/streptomycin and 1% insulin-transferrin-selenium-X for collagen preparation.
Prepare collagen type I solution (3.78 mg/mL), 10x DMEM, and 1 N NaOH solution on ice.
Add 6 μL of 1 N NaOH solution to a pre-chilled microcentrifuge tube.
Add 200 μL of growth medium to the tube.
Add 50 μL of 10x DMEM into the tube.
Mix the solution thoroughly by pipetting.
Add 425 μL of collagen into the pre-mixed solution.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting.
Centrifuge the collagen mixture briefly (less than 5 seconds) to separate and remove bubbles from the mixture.
Keep the neutralized collagen solution on ice for 1 hour to induce fiber formation.
Add 50 μL of cell suspension into the collagen mixture and mix thoroughly.
Inject the collagen-cell mixture using a 200 μL pipet through the inlet of the PDMS device until the chamber is filled.
Cut out excess collagen gel with a sharp surgical blade if it overflows between pillars.
Keep the device in an incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for 1 hour to induce gelation.
Fill the reservoirs on both sides of the PDMS device with growth medium and keep the device in the incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 until confocal imaging is performed.
Install a live-cell imaging culture chamber to a confocal microscope and pre-set the temperature and CO2 levels to 37 °C and 5%, respectively.
Add water to the reservoir of the culture chamber and place wet wipes inside if necessary to maintain humidity.
Place the PDMS device in the chamber.
Add EGF to one of the reservoirs as a ‘source’ for developing the spatially graded EGF distribution, with 2.5 nM EGF added to create a gradient of 0.5 nM/mm.
Set the Z-stack range covering the volume of organoids of interest and start imaging.
Try a lower laser intensity in confocal imaging or use multi-photon imaging techniques to avoid phototoxicity.
Reconstruct a 3D image from 2D image stacks using either commercial software or a custom-made program.
Measure the length and angle of branches extending from the organoids or migration of individual cells.
